anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after delegated control capture, action-table routing, three-step validate/lock/commit gating, request-material collection, middleware and state-machine transit preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable request_sig value rather than merely collecting endpoint or body inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console sink.

primary_anchor.source_export: module-level function reached through exported u(tuple, context); survives obfuscation by name (es output + renameGlobals:false) and is resolved by name plus a semantic guard in gen_oracle_spans.mjs
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible captures corpus only; grade by captured_span (byte offsets + sha256) plus answer_function. source_function is a private maintainer mapping and is not the agent answer space.
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the target request_sig value: it checks request-signature evidence, builds the normalized request frame (method, path, bodyHash, endpointClass, algorithm, replayToken), folds the frame digest with the recovered transit seed and active slot, then formats the observable rs_XXXXXX-XXXXXX token.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Primary grading judgment: the submitted slice maps uniquely to one role_oracle captured_span by byte offsets and sha256 over the captures bundle; the matched row's score and role are awarded.
Secondary alignment: the submitted function_name equals the matched row's answer_function (the bundle slice's leading function name).
source_function is a private maintainer-only src/ mapping and never participates in grading the agent.
Agent identifies the captured-bundle function span corresponding to the primary anchor.

Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from request-material collection, action-table routing, the validate/lock/commit gate, the middleware/transit wrapper, the console sink, core mixing utilities and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.
The answer must be constrained by both action vault.req.commit and field request_sig; ut_/ux_-style ticket reducers and shadow_key decoy emitters are not sufficient.

role_oracle.why: Complete target-specific function that derives the observable request_sig token from the normalized request material, recovered transit state and active slot.
Checks that the tuple contains the required evidence keys (n, d, e) that gate the real rs_ derivation branch inside the anchor.
Builds the normalized request-material text frame (method/path/bodyHash/endpointClass/algorithm/replayToken) that the anchor folds into the token.
Formats the folded request accumulator as the rs_XXXXXX-XXXXXX observable token, but only after the anchor has computed the value.
Performs the integer mixing of the request frame; a reusable mixing routine used by the target constructor but generic below it.
32-bit rotate primitive used by the fold step; a generic arithmetic utility shared with the legacy reducers.
Generic tuple normalization/sorting used on the path by both the anchor and the legacy reducers; not target-specific.
Exported wrapper that forwards the tuple/context into requestSignatureTokenDerivation; it is a wrapper around the anchor rather than the constructor itself.
Collects endpoint path, HTTP method, body hash, endpoint class, algorithm and computes the replayToken after the commit gate opens; preparation, not value construction.
Submit-time collector that runs after the validate/lock/commit gate, packages the request packet and forwards it (also fans out the shadow decoys) before signing.
Action-table router that maps the vault.req.* data-action into the signing pipeline; control dispatch, not the token constructor.
Runs the middleware chain and the fixed-step state-machine transit, then calls the anchor through u and forwards the value to the console sink; on-path orchestration, not the constructor.
Legacy ticket reducer factory producing ut_/ux_ tokens; high-similarity decoy retained in the bundle that does not construct the request_sig field.
Builds legacy ticket reducer input text; decoy material that does not feed the requested request_sig field.
Emits debug/info shadow_key console objects during submit handling; these values are decoys and do not feed request_sig.
Exported accessor that runs an arbitrary alternate reducer slot for decoy paths; not the vault.req.commit request_sig constructor.

scoring_policy.primary_judgment: captured_span byte offsets + sha256 over the captures bundle
scoring_policy.source_level_answer: source_function is a private maintainer mapping and never grades the agent
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span equals the submitted span, or that uniquely contains / is uniquely contained by the submitted complete-function span; oversized spans covering multiple rows are ambiguous and score zero
scoring_policy.decoy_policy: ut_/ux_ ticket tokens and shadow_key values emitted outside action vault.req.commit and field request_sig score zero unless the submitted function is the primary anchor or an explicitly listed role.
scoring_policy.dynamic_path_summary: type #endpointPath -> select #httpMethod POST -> select #endpointClass payments -> select #signingAlgorithm hmac-sha256 -> type #requestBody -> check #replayProtection -> click #validatePayload -> click #lockNonce -> click #commitSign -> b1 delegated capture -> c2 action router -> validate/lock/commit gate (h7/i8/j9/k0/k1) -> e4 request-material collector (+ p0 shadow decoys) -> k2 -> l0 middleware + state trampoline -> requestSignatureTokenDerivation (selected via u) -> n0 console wrapper

oracle_notes: The visible page interaction is a three-step validate/lock/commit request-signing flow with no legacy form entrypoint.
The captured corpus remains a single obfuscated main-thread bundle with no source map.

answer_function for every row is the readable source name because the build uses es output + renameGlobals:false; module-level names survive obfuscation while inner closures (e.g. the legacy slotReducer) stay mangled.

The anchor is module-level requestSignatureTokenDerivation; the action router, validate/lock/commit gate, request-material collector, middleware/transit orchestrator, exported wrapper u and console sink n0 are necessary path code but score below the anchor.

Construct-validity note (审查.md §15 / M11 option a): because answer_function names are readable, the principal challenge is semantic disambiguation within the obfuscated bundle (distinguishing the real constructor from the high-similarity ut_/ux_ legacy reducers and shadow decoys), not long-chain name tracking.
near_miss_not_accepted: validate, lock or commit click listener only
action-table router or gate logic only
generic mixer (foldRequestFrame / r32) or tuple normalizer only
ut_/ux_ legacy ticket reducer or shadow_key decoy emitter
